speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: asked 	the Minister for Social and Family Development whether there has been an increase in ComCare assistance cases compared to last year.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: So, I am a little bit surprised that the numbers have come down somewhat.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: I would also like to ask the Senior Parliamentary Secretary whether the Social Service Offices (SSOs) which have been in operation for some time, whether the fact that they do not operate during weekends, is that something which should be reviewed as a way to reach out to the people who may need help, particularly during weekends?

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The SSOs which have been developed over the years have come to a situation whereby the numbers have stabilised and we are able to reach out to be more accessible to fellow Singaporeans.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Also, because of the increase in numbers as well as the criteria that are given, we are happy to be able to help our fellow Singaporeans.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, while the numbers have decreased, it also shows that we have come to a situation whereby we are able to reach out and the numbers have stabilised in terms of the number of SSOs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We are in a position to be able to help Singaporeans when they need it.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Also, we want to make sure that the lifestyle of caring becomes pervasive and it is a norm among Singaporeans.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: When I look at the figure, I feel very happy because while in terms of the situation that we have here, but yet we are able to reach out to fellow Singaporeans and make sure those who cannot find a job, we help them to find a job, and those who need help, we get not only our ComCare avenues to help, but get the community to help each and every one Singaporean.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Some of them, of course, are not very mobile or have chronic conditions.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: It is a very important question because, like what I have shared with Mr Seah earlier, it is not only the role of the SSOs, I am happy to see community leaders, grassroots leaders, working together with Government agencies to help our fellow Singaporeans.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: It is something that I want to assure the House that we will do all we can to help fellow Singaporeans.
